UAE Retail Industry Faces Credit Freeze, Store Closures Amid Financial Crisis

DUBAI, June 12 – The United Arab Emirates’ retail sector is in turmoil as a severe credit freeze grips the industry, halting expansion plans and forcing widespread store closures, industry officials said on Wednesday.

Retailers across the country, from major chains to smaller outlets, are struggling to secure new lines of credit and refinance existing debt, according to the UAE Retailers Association. “Banks have dramatically tightened lending standards, and many of our members are unable to access the liquidity they need to maintain operations,” said Association Chair Faisal Al Mazrouei.

At least 140 retail outlets have closed in Dubai and Abu Dhabi since May, with dozens more reportedly shuttered in Sharjah and other Emirates. “We had to let go of 80 staff in the past two weeks,” said Mariam Saleh, human resources manager at the supermarket chain Urban Mart. “We simply couldn’t meet payroll without access to credit.”

Footfall in shopping malls has declined sharply, and discounting has done little to revive demand, retailers said. Analysts estimate that retail sales in May dropped 18% year-on-year, with electronics and clothing outlets particularly hard hit.

“The sector is approaching a breaking point,” said Amir Khan, senior analyst at Gulf Markets Research. “If the credit freeze continues, more retailers will be forced to downsize or shut down entirely.”

Union leaders expressed concern for workers, noting reports of unpaid wages and canceled shifts. “Thousands of jobs are at risk,” said Noor Al Habsi of the Retail Workers Union. “We urge immediate action to support employees and stabilize the industry.”
